correctness.rationale: Oddness of F and the charge update give q=-x/2 exactly and one primitive antipodal orbit per positive root of sin(Phi_b(x))=-x/a, with 0<x<=a. The residual is analytic past the compact counting interval and its derivative at zero is pi(1+b)+1/a>0, so the number is finite at every finite a. On a fixed prefix the two phases Phi_b +/- arcsin(x/a) have bounded range and are strictly concave for sufficiently large a, giving O_b(1) crossings. Beyond a fixed L with Phi_b'<0 the minus phase decreases; the plus phase has derivative sign 1-h_a(x), where h_a=-Phi_b'(x)*sqrt(a^2-x^2) has at most one maximum, starts above 1 at L and ends at 0. The terminal rise in the plus phase is at most pi/2, because Phi_b still decreases. Hence each family counts the phase drop -Phi_b(a) divided by 2pi with bounded rounding, turning-point and endpoint corrections. The excluded origin and possible shared endpoint alter the count by at most two. Recomputing the derivative gives J at both antipodes with trace 1-s and determinant -gamma*s, gamma>1 on x>=L, s=a*pi*cos(Phi_b)*[bx^2/4-(1+b)]. On [L,ca], |s| tends uniformly to infinity. For s>0 the characteristic polynomial is negative at both -1 and 1; for s<0 it is positive at 1 with trace >2 and determinant >1, so either both real roots exceed 1 or the conjugate pair has modulus >1. The two-step derivative is J^2. The same crossing count restricted to [L,ca] gives a fraction tending to c^3, and c can approach 1. This checks the fixed-b asymptotics, not finite-gain uniformity in b or other periods. The supplied numerical checker was inspected, not run, and is not needed for the proof.
